From: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@helionhealth.com>

Cc: Michael Yang <michael.yang@helionhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: chain-of-custody confirmation and quick integrity check

Mina —

Following the incident on 2026-01-07, Helion's internal audit team has asked us to get a short, written confirmation from Redwood that: (1) there was no data exfiltration involving our tenant data, and (2) you can provide chain-of-custody or hash reconciliation for the logs and S3 objects that touch our account for the window 2026-01-07 02:30Z — 2026-01-07 03:45Z.

Specific asks:
- A statement confirming whether Helion data was accessed or exported outside Redwood controls.
- Hash reconciliation or signed checksums for the S3 prefixes and the audit-log slices for the time window above.
- Any sampling results for processed request payloads (we need assurance there was no PHI in logs accessible outside the cluster).
- Estimated delivery timeline for the evidence packet (PDF + CSV hashes + sampling notes).

We need this for our SOC audit next week. Can you confirm receipt and provide an ETA?

Thanks —
Emma

Thanks for the clear asks. We've started an internal evidence collection and triage. High-level plan and ETA:

- 48 hours: complete automated hash reconciliation and a first-pass sampling report.
- 72 hours: consolidate forensic packet (PDF summary, csv of hashes, sampling notes).

Preliminary note: our initial checks of network and cluster telemetry show no outbound connections to external storage endpoints from tenant runtime nodes during that window. We'll confirm that with signed hashes.

Deliverables will include: a short attestation statement, the reconciliation CSV, and a sampling summary. We'll also provide a one-page timeline of actions taken during the incident. I will deliver the packet to the Drive link below and share a Doc for your audit team.

Drive folder (working): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D-helion-evidence

Emma / Michael —

Attached is the finalized evidence packet from Redwood for the window 2026-01-07 02:30Z — 2026-01-07 03:45Z. Summary below; full artifacts are in the Drive folder (link repeated).

Summary (short):
- Attestation: No customer data belonging to Helion Health was exported from Redwood infrastructure to any external endpoint controlled outside Redwood between 2026-01-07T02:30:00Z and 2026-01-07T03:45:00Z. This statement is based on network egress telemetry, object-store access logs, and process-level access traces.
- Hash reconciliation: We computed SHA256 checksums for the S3 prefixes and the corresponding audit-log slices. All computed checksums match the signed store snapshots we maintain; no tampering detected. See s3_hash_reconciliation_20260112.csv.
- Log sampling: We performed a randomized sample (0.5% of request payloads touching Helion tenant IDs during the window). No PHI or user-identifiable fields were found outside expected masked fields. See log_sampling_summary_helion.txt.
- Chain-of-custody: Forensic_report_redwood_helion_stub.pdf includes a mapping of evidence collection steps, operator IDs, timeline, and the cryptographic seal used when we captured the snapshots.

Attachments (in Drive and attached as stubs): forensic_report_redwood_helion_stub.pdf; s3_hash_reconciliation_20260112.csv; log_sampling_summary_helion.txt

Next steps we recommend for Helion:
- For your audit, use the attached cover letter (prepared by Marissa) alongside the forensic packet.
- If you'd like a live walkthrough, propose two 20-minute slots and we'll schedule.

Drive folder (final): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C4D-helion-evidence

If you need any more technical detail (raw telemetry, full log slices under NDA), we can produce those under a scoped request.

Attestation signed by: Mina Haddad (Senior Security Engineer) and on behalf of Redwood Inference.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
